A version 1 config.json (or one with general/settings/clipboard/automation/island) is `legacy`: its settings sections become settings.json's (`settings` as `windows`) unless settingsInput is given, which wins; `legacy` is what it said about Slate files. `error` and `errorFile` when a file can't be read; `encodeError` when the value decodes but JSON can't hold it. UUIDs Swift generated for entries without an id read "RANDOM-UUID". `decode`: one config.json each, as a version 1 file with everything in it; `files`: both files.
